newsitem.title: USA: Apple to release new Mac software next week.
newsitem.headline: Apple to release new Mac software next week.

text.p: Fans of the Macintosh computer may finally have something to celebrate next week.

Apple Computer Inc. on Tuesday is set to unveil Mac OS 8, a new version of the basic software that controls the Macintosh computer. The programme, to be priced between $70 and $100, could prompt many existing Macintosh users to upgrade, generating some much-needed revenue for the company, analysts said.

Mac OS 8 improves the performance of Apple computers, simplifies basic tasks, makes it easier to connect to the Internet and fixes some of the minor glitches of predecessor versions, Apple said. The product is the biggest overhaul of the Macintosh since 1991, when it did a major revamping.

"We are really optimistic that Mac OS 8 is going to get a lot of people to upgrade," said Peter Lowe, Apple product manager for Mac OS 8. "We believe the combination of the new software with the hardware offerings we have today is going to have a really significant impact on our business."
Rob Enderle, analyst at market researcher Giga Information Group, said: "Upgrades do produce a spike in revenue."
Mac OS 8 also is expected to tide over software developers until Apple introduces an entirely new generation of Macintosh computers next year based on a programme code-named Rhapsody, analysts said.

Some independent software companies had complained that Apple had not done enough to improve the Mac's software foundation to set it clearly apart from Microsoft Corp.'s family of Windows operating systems.
The popularity of Windows surged in 1995, when Microsoft began shipping Windows 95, which included many innovations that the Macintosh had introduced 10 years earlier.

Apple said the improvements in Mac OS 8, compared with its predecessor System 7.6, include better reliability, easier connection options to the Internet, better handling of simultaneous tasks and new options for juggling icons and menus.
